study: Trader Bro call-outs as BOOK names: once a name is called it stays on the book for the rest of the session, and the trade waits for the operator's signal: not in or just under a known resistance block AND %R trending up. Does that signal beat the spread, and beat a random minute while the name is on the book?
registered_at: 2026-10-07, before any S/R or %R feature is computed on the call archive
origin: Operator 10/7: 'once we receive the name, check the SR gap; if it is not in resistance or close to it, check %R for trending'. Prior study BB_LIVE_CALLOUTS_2026-09-27.md (1,730 calls, 34 sessions): buying the next minute after a call lost after costs (actionable -106/-246 bp at 15 min), with huge two-sided moves (median MFE30 +8%, MAE30 -8.5%); the call minute did not beat a random later minute. Operator 10/7 (follow-up): 'always keeping those suggestions ... on the book ready to trade for those signals' -> the PRIMARY is the on-book signal, not the call moment.
data: ai_reports/bb_live.jsonl on the mini (2,188 rows, 2026-08-10..2026-10-06 at registration) plus any sessions captured before the run; deduped on (ticker, text, second); OCR noise rows whose ticker is not a tradable US common stock are dropped (counted)
calls: PRIMARY population: the first ACTIONABLE call per symbol-day (actionable = ai_entry_watch._bb_call_is_actionable is True). Receive time R = the archive's capture timestamp 'unix' (when the desk could first act), not the spoken minute.

features_at_R.SR_ok: NOT ob_resist_0.3: price at R is not inside, and not within 0.3% under, a charted resistance block (unbroken bearish OB or bullish breaker; tools/order_blocks.py, swing 10, wicks, last 3 per side) KNOWN before R, computed on SIP 1-minute bars (prior day + day, 04:00-16:00) closed before R
features_at_R.WR_trending: fast %R (21, EMA 7) of the last 1-min bar closed before R is higher than 3 bars earlier AND slow %R (112, EMA 3) is higher than 3 bars earlier (both rising); same SIP bars
features_at_R.note: for the PRIMARY the same features are evaluated at each 1-min close t after R, not only at R

entry_exit.entry: the first SIP trade at or after R + 2 s (regular-hours or extended), price = that trade; cost = full SIP NBBO spread at R (half in, half out)
entry_exit.primary_outcome: net15 = last SIP trade at or before entry time + 15 min / entry - 1 - spread

statistic: mean net15 per call; day-clustered t; halves = alternate sessions (A even, B odd index)
power: report SE and MDE = 2.84 x SE for the PRIMARY per half before any mean; MDE > 150 bp -> UNDERPOWERED for the historical run; the forward record then decides
pass: Each group separately (Bonferroni 2: t >= 2.24): PRIMARY net15 > 0 with day-clustered t >= 2.24 in BOTH halves, AND PRIMARY minus CONTROL (paired) >= +50 bp with t >= 2.24 pooled, AND >= 60 PRIMARY entries per half; otherwise FAIL, or UNDERPOWERED per the power rule. A T pass earns a paper A/B of the on-book signal for $10+ Trader Bro names; an S pass earns a paper A/B of a LOWER PRICE FLOOR ($2) for Trader Bro names only, with the spread cap reviewed separately. INFO_at_call is information only.
forward: both groups are logged and scored on every new session from 2026-10-08 (held-out); scored when a group reaches >= 60 entries per half (T will take months at ~0.75 tradeable calls/day)
no_retuning: the 0.3% band, the 3-bar %R slope, the 2 s latency, the 15-min hold and the population are fixed here
prior: LOW: the call moment lost on 34 sessions; S/R filters (10/02, 10/05, 10/06) and %R triggers never separated entries; but this combination on call-outs is untested
caveats: capture time can lag the spoken call by seconds
SIP history vs the live IEX feed
34-40 sessions: only large effects are detectable
call text is free-form; 'actionable' removes only clear exits/passes

design.PRIMARY_on_book: from receive time R until 15:30 ET, at every 1-min close t (09:30-15:30) evaluate SR_ok AND WR_trending using only data closed by t; the FIRST minute PASS holds is the entry decision (one entry per name-day). Entry = the first SIP trade at or after t + 2 s; outcome net15 as below.
design.CONTROL_on_book: per PRIMARY entry, one random 1-min close (seed 53) in the same name-day that is NOT a PASS minute and starts AFTER the PRIMARY trade has exited (entry + 15 min) and by 15:30; same entry/exit/cost rule. Controls are never drawn before or during the signal trade, because those windows contain the rise that produced the signal (the 10/06 hindsight-control artifact). Pairs with no eligible control are dropped and counted.
design.INFO_at_call: the call moment itself: entry at R + 2 s, with SR_ok/WR_trending reported as a split (the operator's first phrasing)

amended: 2026-10-07, before any feature was computed: operator follow-up makes the on-book signal the primary and the call moment information; control restricted to minutes after the PRIMARY exit (hindsight guard); operator 10/7: primary counts only desk-tradeable calls (T), with $2-10 calls scored separately (S) as the floor-change candidate; under $2 excluded

groups.T_tradeable: calls whose price at the entry decision is >= $10 AND SIP spread <= 0.05% (the desk's current floor and cap). The desk's real use. Count check at registration: only 31 of 643 first-actionable name-days had a captured price >= $10, so the historical run is expected UNDERPOWERED; forward logging continues.
groups.S_floor_candidate: calls priced $2-$10 at the entry decision (any spread), costed at each name's real SIP spread. Decides whether lowering the price floor for Trader Bro names is worth a paper A/B.
